summary: The original feature was implemented upstream by merged PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19354, but later runnable diffusion tests reintroduced 20 hard-coded copies of model IDs already centralized in test_utils.py. This change replaces those copies in generic GPU, Ascend/ModelScope, MUSA, request-logging, and data-parallel test entries, and adds a regression guard that rejects executable duplicates while permitting unit-test vectors and documentation strings.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: found 20 executable hard-coded duplicates of canonical diffusion model IDs in the recorded base. The nonzero exit is expected evidence of the pre-change regression.

Two tests passed: the complete runnable diffusion test tree contains no duplicated canonical model literals, and an adversarial fixture proves executable literals are rejected while docstrings are ignored.
All repository-pinned hooks applicable to the touched files passed, including Python AST validation, isort, Ruff lint/format, codespell, secret detection, and diffusion test policy checks.
Collected all four request-logger cases and the two-GPU DP case, validating import and test discovery compatibility after replacing their local model literals.
All modified runnable entry modules compiled successfully with the prepared interpreter.
No whitespace errors in the contribution.

gpu_execution.evidence: No inference or numerical code changed. The assigned node exposes one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), but the directly touched DP runtime test requires two GPUs; the Ascend and MUSA entry paths require unavailable accelerator architectures. Startup smoke or unrelated one-GPU inference would not validate this refactor.

remaining_limitations: The two-GPU data-parallel serving test was collected but not executed because only one GPU was assigned.
Ascend/ModelScope and MUSA runtime cases were not executed because those accelerator architectures are unavailable on this ROCm node.
No model weights were downloaded because this refactor changes test entry references only and model inference would not provide an independent numerical claim relevant to the feature.
Unit tests that intentionally use model-name literals as parser/configuration test vectors remain unchanged and are explicitly outside the runnable-entry regression guard.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
